newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Sept 17.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Sept. 17:
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration was reconsidering whether to send several thousand Army troops to Kuwait because such a warning gesture to Iraq may no longer be necessary.

WASHINGTON - A government report on the June bombing of a U.S. military housing complex in Saudi Arabia faulted the Defence Department for paying insufficient attention to terrorist threats and failing to do enough to protect troops.

WASHINGTON - Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole proposed an anti-crime package that would double spending on new prisons and require prisoners to work, while President Bill Clinton won the endorsement of the nation's largest police organization.
WASHINGTON - Abortion rights activists and their opponents bend the facts in the fight about a controversial procedure sometimes used during the second half of pregnancy, at 20 weeks and beyond.

WASHINGTON - American companies are sending white-collar jobs overseas, using increasingly low-cost satellite and fiber-optic communications to link their U.S. headquarters to much cheaper "back office" operations continents away.
